body:
You are a dialogue writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables, no code fences) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, with no commentary before or after.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Nobody is silly in a way that breaks the setting, and nobody winks at the player. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad.

OUTPUT FORMAT: for each label below write the label on its own line (like "== tudorel_square"), then each line on its own line as `Speaker: text` or `Speaker [mood]: text`. Speakers are exactly the names given. Do not number the lines. Moods are one of: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary; use a mood only where it matters. Where option texts (what the PARTY says) are requested, write them as `* text` rows under that label, under 14 words, in the party's voice ("we", or an imperative).

RULES FOR EVERY LINE: under 190 characters, usually 60 to 130; no braces or placeholders; no em dashes (use commas, full stops or colons); no real-world references; straight apostrophes and quotes; each line should make sense on its own. The Narrator speaks in second person, present tense, one or two sentences, with concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) and no game terms (never "roll", "check", "level", "gold pieces" as a number is fine in speech). Never name the player characters. Use ONLY the facts given here; invent no new named people, places, dates or lore.

CHARACTERS AND FACTS: The Tser Pool camp is a Vistani camp west of the Old Svalich crossroads. The party has turned on it (they drew steel on the Vistani or robbed the elder), so the camp is hostile or empty; do NOT say which, how, or what became of any person there. When the camp is empty the Narrator's existing line is: "The camp is empty. The fire has burned to a red eye in the ashes, and the wagons stand with their doors open. Only the great tent still glows."
Four small unfinished errands each lose the person who would have closed them. No fights, no rolls. The lines below close them quietly.
- Nelu: a thin Vistani boy, Big Tobar's son, who walked off at night after a will-o'-wisp calling him in his dead mother's voice and was three days on a ledge in the gorge under Tser Falls. The party pulled him out. He says things like "Up here in the sun, all that water sounds like nobody at all", and "If anything calls to me in the dark again, I am going to sing over it until my throat gives out." He cannot go back to the Tser Pool camp; the party has brought him instead to the Vistani camp by the lake outside Vallaki's west gate, which Arrigal runs. He knows nothing of why the pool is closed to him, and nobody will tell him.
- Arrigal: a lean, smooth man in a black coat and a silver-buttoned waistcoat who runs the lake camp; unhurried, charming, never says what he wants. Pet idea: "I carry messages." His people count everything and remember decency as well as slights.
- Bujor: a big brown bear who danced for nine years on a plank stage at the pool camp with a young woman, Lavinia, and who broke his chain to guard a bear cub caught in a hunter's iron trap in the clearing at the old den. The party freed the cub and fought off the things that came to the crying.
- Steaua: Radu's grey mare, which Radu sold to the castle's black carriage and the party saved from being turned into a black horse (or, if they failed, lost). The camp's pen stands empty. In the morning after the carriage came there was a purse of old gold at the pen.
- Nicu: Luminita's brother, a young Vistano hanged at the crossroads gallows for a horse he did not steal. The party cut him down and buried him, or put him down again when he rose. They meant to tell his sister Luminita at the pool camp, but she is gone.

STYLE SAMPLES from the existing scenes (match this voice, length and rhythm):
Nelu [weary]: Up here in the sun, all that water sounds like nobody at all.
Nelu [sad]: If anything calls to me in the dark again, I am going to sing over it until my throat gives out.
Arrigal: Welcome, travellers. You're far from the road for honest folk and close to the lake for clever ones. Sit at our fire. It costs nothing, tonight.
Arrigal [smile]: I sell nothing, my friend. I carry messages. Some of them are about you. You'll find our people do the same everywhere in this valley, and live longer for it.
Arrigal: You brought word of Nicu to his people, at the crossroads. That was decently done. We remember decency too.
Narrator: Bujor sways on the plank stage beside Lavinia, slow and heavy and pleased with himself. Under the planks, a bear cub is chewing a boot.
Narrator: He ties a black ribbon to the gate, and doesn't say anything for a long time.
Narrator: Steaua is in the pen when you come back, grey as river stone, with Luminita's face pressed into her neck.
Narrator: You unbuckle the collar. He doesn't wait to be told. He noses the cub up over the stones and into the dark under the rocks, and he doesn't look back, not once.

THE SCENES:

LABELS AND BEATS:
== nelu_away (6 lines: Narrator x2, Nelu x4. The party reaches the lake camp with Nelu. Narrator sets the boy among the Vallaki Vistani, fed and wrapped in somebody's blanket. Nelu says he cannot go home and nobody will say why; he asks, quietly, after his Da, and the party has nothing to tell him; he is thanking them for the ledge, and still singing over the dark. The tone is sad and kind. Do not say where Tobar is.)
== nelu_away_after (2 lines, Nelu, on a later visit: he has stopped asking, sits with his back to the water, and sings over anything that calls.)
== bear_choose_gone (2 lines, Narrator: at the old den, Bujor and the cub are free and he looks down the deer path toward the pool camp. The party looks too: no fiddle, no fire-light, nobody on the plank stage to lead a bear home to.)
== bear_let_go_gone (2 lines, Narrator: after Bujor noses the cub into the den, the party goes back down the deer path. The plank stage at the pool is bare and quiet, and a bear is dancing nowhere. A little sad, a little right.)
== stage_empty (3 lines, Narrator: in the empty pool camp, at the plank stage where Bujor used to dance. Bare boards, a lamp gone out, wind in the leaves; nobody to tell that the bear is safe, or home, or free. The reader can see what was lost. One concrete detail, no lecture.)
== pen_saved (4 lines, Narrator: in the empty horse pen, Steaua stands grey and alone and cross, eating everything in reach; the purse of old gold the carriage left is still on the gatepost; the party takes it, and the mare lets them. Nobody in the camp to say whose she is now.)
== pen_lost (3 lines, Narrator: the empty horse pen, the empty place at the end of it where Steaua stood, a trough of old water. There is no one to tell what the castle made of her. Dry and quiet.)
== arrigal_nicu_option (2 option texts, in the party's voice: they tell Arrigal what became of Nicu at the crossroads, because the camp that should have heard it is gone.)
== arrigal_nicu (5 lines: Narrator x1, Arrigal x4. The party tells Arrigal about Nicu, the gallows, the board that said HORSE THIEF, the burial or the rising. Arrigal listens without a flicker, then says he carries messages, and that this one will go to Nicu's people wherever they are now; he says the lake camp will not forget who told it. No promise about what the news will do. He does not blame the party.)
result:
== nelu_away
Narrator: A woman by the lake fire puts a bowl of hot mutton broth into Nelu's hands and pulls a dry wool blanket around his thin shoulders.
Nelu [weary]: They gave me bread and fat, and a coat that smells like somebody else's horse, and they told me the road back to the pool is shut.
Nelu [sad]: Nobody here says why I cannot go home. Have you seen my Da on the road, or is he only looking for me in the wrong part of the trees?
Narrator: The mist off the lake is cold on your face, and the fire snaps in the quiet while the boy waits for an answer you do not have.
Nelu [sad]: That is all right. You pulled me off the wet rock when the water was loud, and that was work enough for one week.
Nelu: When the mist comes up from the water tonight, I am going to sing every song I know until the dark has no room left to talk.

== nelu_away_after
Nelu [weary]: I sit with my back to the lake now, because water sounds the same everywhere once the sun goes down.
Nelu: I do not ask after the pool camp anymore, and if anything calls my name from the reeds, I sing over it until it gives up.

== bear_choose_gone
Narrator: With the iron off the cub's leg, Bujor stands in the bruised fern and looks down the deer path toward the pool.
Narrator: Nothing comes up through the wet pines to meet him: no fiddle, no woodsmoke, and no girl on the planks to take his chain.

== bear_let_go_gone
Narrator: You walk back down the deer path through the cold smell of pine and turned earth, leaving the rocks and the dark behind you.
Narrator: Below the trees, the plank stage by the pool stands bare to the drizzle, and a big brown bear is dancing for nobody at all.

== stage_empty
Narrator: Rain sits in the nail-holes of the plank stage, and the cold tin lamp on the post smells of dead tallow.
Narrator: Dead leaves have drifted into the hollow under the boards where the cub used to chew on old leather.
Narrator: The wind moves through the alders by the water, and there is no one left in the clearing to hear that the bear got away whole.

== pen_saved
Narrator: Steaua stands alone in the mud of the empty pen, grey and cross, methodically stripping the bark from the top rail.
Narrator: A wet leather purse still hangs from the gatepost where the castle carriage left it, heavy with old gold coins.
Narrator: The mare flattens one ear as you lift the purse from the post, then goes back to chewing the fence.
Narrator: Around you the wagons stand open to the damp air, with nobody left to say whose horse she is now.

== pen_lost
Narrator: The rail pen stands open to the mist, with hoof-prints filling with grey water at the far end where Steaua used to wait.
Narrator: Dead needles float in the wooden trough, and the cold smell of the wet mud is all that is left of the night.
Narrator: There is no one left by the wagons to hear what the black carriage took, or what the castle made of her.

== arrigal_nicu_option
* Tell him what became of Nicu at the crossroads gallows.
* We buried Luminita's brother at the crossroads, and her camp is gone.

== arrigal_nicu
Narrator: Arrigal listens with his hands folded over the silver buttons of his waistcoat, while the lake wind pulls the smoke sideways.
Arrigal: A boy on the crossroads rope with a thief's board around his neck, and strangers to put him in the dirt when the crows were done.
Arrigal: You did not owe him a spade, and you did not owe me the story. Our people remember who brings word when the roads go bad.
Arrigal: I carry messages, my friend. This one will find his sister and his blood, wherever the wagons have stopped tonight.
Arrigal [weary]: What they do with their grief is their own affair, and none of yours, I think. Sit by the fire until the rain lets up.
